cause: OPEN BUG, not yet root-caused. This fixture and default/island_always were riding a run_adjoint reentrancy bug fixed 2026-09-03 (a static thread_local KernelCtx aliased outer and recursively-nested Program::CALL frames -- see runtime/src/adjoint.cpp). That fix eliminated the thousands-to-tens-of-thousands-ULP swings the reentrancy caused, but this pair is still unbounded on Windows (win_amd64, mingw-w64/UCRT64) after the fix: one run agreed to 6 ULP, another to 84,225,866 ULP, a third agreed exactly. No known-clean bound exists yet. Suspected mechanism: no_island runs far more of this fixture's 35 higher-order calls through one flat, ungrouped run_adjoint sequence than default does (which carves most of them into separate islands), so a kernel backward that reads a KernelCtx slot beyond its own call's n_in -- a bug independent of the reentrancy one, since it needs no recursion -- would pick up a stale Desc left by whichever unrelated call ran immediately before it in that flat sequence, with a magnitude bounded only by what garbage that stale pointer happens to reach. Not investigated past this hypothesis. Bitwise on Linux (glibc) and macOS (Apple libm) every run so far.

the 64 per-iteration gradient contributions of a loop whose UDF branches on data are accumulated in a different grouping with and without STANLI_NO_REROLL. Over 40 swept points on macOS neither is more accurate on grad[0] (mean 2.01 against 2.07 ULP, default closer at 7 points and farther at 5); on grad[1] default is closer (mean 0.64 against 0.85).

partition_lanes gathers the scalar terms of the single-row groups into one lane FMA and normal_lpdf (95 ops with the pass, 107 with STANLI_NO_PARTITION), so beta's adjoint adds those rows' contributions in a different grouping. no_partition and passes_off give the same bits, and the retained loop (structured_forced) agrees with default bitwise.

partition_lanes gathers the scalar terms of the single-row groups into one lane FMA and normal_lpdf (95 ops with the pass, 107 with STANLI_NO_PARTITION), so beta's adjoint adds those rows' contributions in a different grouping. no_partition and passes_off give the same bits, and the retained loop (structured_forced) agrees with default bitwise.

Each group's sum(mu[g] + x[rows] * beta) and sum(scaled[rows] * beta) sums a matrix-vector product. The write_array graph forms the product with Eigen (OP_MATVEC, OP_GEMM) and sums it with Eigen's packet reduction (OP_SUM_VEC variant 1). The interpreter forms the product with a scalar loop and, finding no packet access in the expression's source layout, adds the elements in order. Switching both to Eigen in the interpreter gives the graph's bits; switching either one alone does not. Against an 80-digit mpmath reference at draw variant 0 the interpreter is 0.27 ULP off and the graph 1.27 ULP. The default graph unrolls this loop, so the gap does not involve retained loops.

tau's adjoint is the sum of the twelve groups' contributions through scaled[g] = tau * L[g]. The default graph unrolls the loop, and reroll and inplace together add those contributions in a different order; turning off either one gives the passes_off bits, which the retained loop (STANLI_STRUCTURED_LOOPS=1) also gives. Against an 80-digit mpmath reference at draw variant 0 the default graph is 2.18 ULP off and passes_off 0.18 ULP.
